texts.li: The people who walked up from {PLACE} are thin and a little unsteady, and alive. {X_nameDef} is the first of them through the gate. With {TALE} over at last, {FACTION} have sent the first of their well to thank the colony for the medicine, and to bring a gift worth about {COUNT} silver.\n\nThey would also like, if the colony will allow it, to say the names of their dead somewhere other than at home.

[theirHightech] There's a list folded inside the box {X_nameDef} carried up from {PLACE}. The box is a gift from {FACTION}, worth about {COUNT} silver. The list is the names of everyone at {PLACE} who lived through {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} says the colony's medicine is the reason some of them are on it.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} asked for {FRIEND_nameDef} before anything else. At {PLACE}, where {TALE} has finally run its course, that name is known in every house. {FACTION} want to give thanks properly, with a gift worth about {COUNT} silver, and with words said aloud.

[end:someHelp] "You didn't do much," {X_nameDef} says, frankly, "but you did something, when most didn't." With {TALE} over at {PLACE}, {FACTION} want it known that they noticed, and {X_nameDef} has brought a gift worth about {COUNT} silver to say so.

li.label: Accept the gift with thanks
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} sets the gift down and holds {A_nameDef}'s hands in both of {X_possessive} own for a long moment. {FACTION} will tell it at {PLACE} that the colony took their thanks gladly.

li.label: Say the names of their dead together
li.outcome: The colony gathers at dusk with the visitors from {PLACE}, and {X_nameDef} says the names of their dead one by one. It takes a long time, and the colony stays for all of it.

outcomes.li: [trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} stands beside {X_nameDef} while the names are said, and when {X_pronoun} falters, says the last few with {X_objective}.

li.label: Ask them to keep it for {PLACE}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} that {PLACE} needs the gift more than the colony does. {X_nameDef} doesn't argue. {FACTION} will remember that too, {X_pronoun} says, and packs the gift up again.

texts.li: [theirLowtech] The sacks carried up from {PLACE} are full, and for once so are the people carrying them. The first harvest since {TALE} is in, and {FACTION} keep a custom of sending the first of it to whoever fed them in the hungry year.\n\n{X_nameDef} has brought {COUNT} measures of {THING}, and won't take no for an answer.

[theirHightech] {FACTION}'s first harvest since {TALE} is in, and {X_nameDef} has come up from {PLACE} with a share of it: {COUNT} measures of {THING}, as thanks for the food that got them through. Their trucks are running on real fuel again, {X_nameDef} adds, which is how everyone at {PLACE} knows things are better.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING} from the first harvest after {TALE}, and asks for {FRIEND_nameDef}. The custom is to put the first grain in the hands of whoever helped most.

li.label: Accept the grain
li.outcome: The grain goes into the colony's stores, and {X_nameDef} sets off home the same afternoon, with planting still to do.

li.label: Bake it into a harvest supper, with them
li.outcome: The colony keeps the grain and sets the long table tonight, with {X_nameDef} at the head of it. It's the first full meal {X_nameDef} has eaten away from home in a year, {X_pronoun} says.

li.label: the supper of the first harvest
Send it on to someone hungrier
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} asks {X_nameDef} to take the grain to the next village down the road, where the harvest failed again. {X_nameDef} looks at {A_objective} a moment, then shoulders the first sack again.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} and the others from {PLACE} have searched every bank and sandbar between their town and the colony. What {TALE} carried off was the bell from their meeting hall, the one that rang for every wedding and every fire for a hundred years, and {FACTION} want it back.\n\nA few weeks ago the colony's people pulled something heavy and green out of the shallows. It has been sitting in the stores ever since.

[theirHightech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up the river looking for what {TALE} took from {PLACE}: the town's founding plaque, bronze, the size of a door. {X_nameDef} doesn't expect to find it.\n\nIt's leaning against a wall in the colony's stores, where someone left it after dragging it out of the mud.

[ignored] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} doesn't ask the colony for anything. {FACTION} stopped expecting it to give during {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} has only come up from {PLACE} because the banks below the colony are the last place left to search.\n\nThere is a waterlogged bell in the colony's stores that came out of the river last month.

li.label: Give it back to them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stares at it for a long time, then sits down on the ground and laughs until {X_pronoun} cries. {FACTION} will carry it home on a pole between them, singing most of the way.

li.label: Let them buy it back
li.outcome: {FACTION} pay what the bronze is worth, which is a lot, and carry it home. They'll remember the price as well as the bell.

li.label: Help them carry it home
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and a couple of strong backs carry it down to {PLACE} themselves, and stay for the first ringing. {FACTION} feed them until they can hardly walk.

texts.li: [flag:sheltered] Two travelers of {FACTION} sat out {TALE} by the colony's hearth, and promised {A_nameDef} they would repay it when the roads opened. The roads are open. They've come back with the mud of the thaw on their boots and {COUNT} measures of {THING} for planting, the best in {PLACE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} would like to help put it in the ground, too.

[helped] The colony's firewood kept {PLACE} warm through the worst of {TALE}. Now the roads are open, and {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come up with {COUNT} measures of {THING} for the spring planting, by way of thanks.

li.label: Accept the seed with thanks
li.outcome: The seed goes into the colony's stores, and the visitors eat a hot meal by the same hearth they sat at all winter, which they say tastes better with the door open.

li.label: Plant it together, out in the fields
li.outcome: The visitors roll up their sleeves, and the colony goes out to the fields with them to work the first of the seed into the ground.

li.label: Tell them the debt is long paid
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sends the seed back with them for their own fields. They argue, then laugh, then go.

texts.li: [locusts] {COUNT} measures of {THING} is enough to sow the colony's fields again, and that is what {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has carried up from {PLACE}. They heard what {TALE} did, and they have not forgotten the colony's good turns.

[famine|drought] It has been a lean year since {TALE}, for the colony as much as anyone. {FACTION} remember who stood by them once. {X_nameDef} has come from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING}, and would be insulted by an offer of payment.

[their:friend] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come from {PLACE} with {COUNT} measures of {THING} for the colony, after {TALE}. It was {FRIEND_nameDef} who did their people a good turn once, {X_nameDef} says; this is the turn coming back.

[their:rescued] {FACTION} haven't forgotten what the colony did for their people, and they know what {TALE} cost it. {X_nameDef} has brought {COUNT} measures of {THING} from {PLACE}, and a message from the elders, that friends don't wait to be asked.

li.label: Accept, with thanks
li.outcome: The seed goes into the stores. {X_nameDef} won't take anything for it, and is on the road home by noon.

li.label: Accept, and feast their messenger
li.outcome: The seed goes into the stores and {X_nameDef} goes to the head of the table. It's a thin feast in a thin year, and the talk makes up for it.

li.label: Ask them to give it to {PLACE}'s own hungry
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony will manage, and that {PLACE} surely has hungry people of its own. {X_nameDef} goes home as loaded as {X_pronoun} came, with a story to tell.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, an elder of {FACTION}, has walked from {PLACE} to say something to the colony's face, and says it without raising {X_possessive} voice. One by one, {X_nameDef} names the people {PLACE} buried during {TALE}. Then the day the colony's gate stayed shut.\n\nThen {X_nameDef} waits to see what the colony will say.

[end:profiteer] In {X_nameDef}'s account book, in neat columns, is what {FACTION} paid the colony for food during {TALE}, and beside it what that food was worth. {X_nameDef}, an elder of theirs, has carried the book up from {PLACE}.\n\n{X_nameDef} doesn't ask for anything. The figures are read out, column by column, and then {X_nameDef} waits.

[their:grudge] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has come to the gate, and {FACTION} haven't forgiven the colony much lately. {PLACE} remembers who looked away during {TALE}, {X_nameDef} says, and has sent {X_objective} to hear what the colony has to say about it.

li.label: Make amends ({COUNT} silver for {PLACE})
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} puts {COUNT} silver into {X_nameDef}'s hands for {PLACE}'s widows, and says the colony was wrong. {X_nameDef} weighs the purse, and then the words, and nods once.

li.label: Hear them out, and say sorry in front of everyone
li.outcome: The colony gathers to hear {X_nameDef}, and {A_nameDef} answers in front of all of them: the colony was wrong, and will do better. A few of the colony keep their eyes on the ground through all of it.

li.label: The colony owes {PLACE} nothing
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} tells {X_nameDef} the colony looked after its own, as anyone would. {X_nameDef} says {FACTION} will remember that answer, and walks home.
